All About HAST
New for 2025: Model EHS-222-L with eight-inch deeper test area
HAST (Highly Accelerated Stress Test) chambers reduce the time it takes to complete humidity testing for semiconductors. By elevating temperatures above 100°C and increasing the pressure, simulation of normal humidity tests can be made while maintaining the same failure mechanisms. Tests can be completed in days, not weeks. Our HAST systems have a modern design that's easier to use:
Automatic humidity filling
Automatic door lock
A round workspace, allowing wider sample boards to be loaded
Convenient, hermetic power-pin system for bias testing
We now offer an "Air HAST" modification for faster testing of lead-free solder whisker resistance to humidity.
 Features for HAST - Highly Accelerated Stress Test Chambers 
Unsaturated or saturated humidity control
Multi-mode 'M' system controls humidity (via wet bulb/dry bulb), even during heat-up and cool-down. Fully conforms to EIA/JEDEC test method A110 & 102C.
Touch-screen controller with temperature, humidity, and count-down display
Ethernet interface for remote access, data downloads, and email alerts
Language selection of English, Japanese, Chinese, or Korean
Specimen power terminals, allow power-up of specimens
Cabinet Features:
Inner cylinder and door shield protect specimens from dew condensation
Interior is cylindrical for maximum product loading
Two stainless steel shelves
Set of casters for easy movement of the chamber (except double units)
Safety Features:
Overheat & over-pressure protectors
Door lock safety mechanism to prevent opening of the door while the chamber is pressurized
Specimen power control terminal: shuts down the product power in the event of an alarm

What is a HAST Chamber?
Highly Accelerated Stress Test (HAST) chambers are specialized environmental test chambers that simulate years of real-world humidity and bias stress in just days. By combining high temperatures (typically above 100°C), elevated humidity (up to 100% RH), and positive pressure, HAST chambers rapidly accelerate failure mechanisms in electronic components—uncovering potential issues before your products reach the field.
Typically, HAST testing is used to accelerate testing done at 85°C/85%RH. The primary consideration to stepping up to HAST would be the product’s ability to withstand temperatures over 100°C without changes in failure modes.
Think of HAST as an Instant Pot pressure cooker, where elevated temperature and pressure speeds cooking. In fact, the first HAST tests 40 years ago were done with simple pressure cookers. But repeatability and condensation issues led to the further refinement of HAST chambers.
How Does HAST Work?
High Temperature: Exposes components to conditions well above standard operation, revealing heat-related failure points.
High Humidity: Promotes corrosion and insulation breakdown—critical for detecting moisture-sensitive weaknesses.
Pressure: Increases the rate of chemical reactions, speeding up aging and stress effects.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
How does Air-HAST differ from standard HAST?
Air-HAST introduces controlled oxygen into the chamber, allowing for accelerated studies of oxidation and solder whisker phenomena—critical for advanced electronics and lead-free assemblies.
Can I run bias testing in your chambers?
Absolutely. Our specimen power terminals allow for safe, reliable bias testing, with automatic shutoff if any alarm condition occurs.
What support is available after purchase?
Our global service team provides installation, training, calibration, and technical support—backed by real engineers who understand your challenges.
How do I know which model is right for me?
There are two sizes and two ranges of performance. Some test standards need the higher temperature/pressure range. Contact our applications team for a personalized consultation. We’ll help you choose based on your sample size, compliance needs, and budget.
Are your chambers easy to install?
Yes! Most models are plug-and-play with onboard water tanks and casters for easy movement.
